title: Poincare trace and cup-product pairing
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]: distinct primes $p,\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its fixed algebraic closure $k$, and $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$ with a chosen algebraic closure $\Qlb$. Let $X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper and geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses]. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a_X:X\to s$.

Use the coefficient objects, cohomology and point functor of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], the Tate twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and the derived pullback, tensor and Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Thus $\Ql_X$ is the rationalized completed coefficient unit, not the discrete non-torsion constant sheaf on the small etale site. Write $Ra_{X*}$ for [def-weil-derived-direct-image], $Ra_{X!}$ for the rational-stage construction of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and $Ra_X^!$ for the constructible exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Its constructible adjunction supplies the counit $\varepsilon:Ra_{X!}Ra_X^!\Ql_s\to\Ql_s$; no ambient pro-etale exceptional-adjoint datum is assumed. Fix an orientation isomorphism
$$\eta_X:Ra_X^!\Ql_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Ql_X(d)[2d].$$
All the following traces are relative to this chosen isomorphism.

Define the oriented derived trace by the actual composite
$$T_X:Ra_{X!}(\Ql_X(d)[2d])
 \xrightarrow{Ra_{X!}(\eta_X^{-1})}Ra_{X!}Ra_X^!\Ql_s
 \xrightarrow{\varepsilon}\Ql_s.$$
Applying $H^0\operatorname{Fib}_s$ and the shift comparison gives
$$\operatorname{tr}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\Ql(d))\longrightarrow\Ql.$$
Here $H_c^{2d}(X,\Ql(d))=H^0\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X!}(\Ql_X(d)[2d]))$ uses the cohomological shift convention.

To specify untwisting, put $L=\Ql(d)$ at the coefficient point. This is a one-dimensional line; negative twists are its dual, using [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and the rank-one twist property [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. Use the projection isomorphism [fix-prop-projection-formula] at $(a_X,\Ql_X,\Ql_s(d))$, the pullback identification $La_X^*\Ql_s(d)=\Ql_X(d)$, and the point tensor identification [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. They specify
$$\phi:H_c^{2d}(X,\Ql)\otimes_{\Ql}L\xrightarrow{\sim}H_c^{2d}(X,\Ql(d)).$$
Define $\tau_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\Ql)\to L^\vee=\Ql(-d)$ by
$$\tau_X(v)(t)=\operatorname{tr}_X(\phi(v\otimes t)).$$
For the proper $X$, let $\kappa:Ra_{X!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{X*}$ be the canonical proper comparison [prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence], and write $h_n=H^n\operatorname{Fib}_s(\kappa_{\Ql_X})$. Define the ordinary untwisted trace by
$$\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X=\tau_X\circ h_{2d}^{-1}:
H^{2d}(X,\Ql)\longrightarrow\Ql(-d).$$

The multiplication $m:\Ql_X\otimes^L_{\Ql}\Ql_X\to\Ql_X$ defines the ordinary cup product with the following explicit support convention. Use the mixed-support product $\mu_c$ of [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product] at $K=L=\Ql_X$, and the proper comparison $h_n$ just fixed. For $x\in H^i(X,\Ql)$, $y\in H^j(X,\Ql)$ set
$$x\smile y=h_{i+j}\bigl(H_c^{i+j}(m)(\mu_c(h_i^{-1}x,y))\bigr).$$
Here $\mu_c$ on classes is induced by its displayed morphism of coefficient complexes: tensor representatives $\Ql[-i]\to R\Gamma_c(X,\Ql)$ and $\Ql[-j]\to R\Gamma(X,\Ql)$ and then compose with that morphism. All maps are $\Ql$-linear in each input, so this defines
$$\smile:H^i(X,\Ql)\otimes_{\Ql}H^j(X,\Ql)\longrightarrow H^{i+j}(X,\Ql)\qquad(i,j\in\mathbf Z).$$
Graded commutativity is the separate property recorded in [lem-pod-cup-product-graded-commutativity], a forward reference rather than an assumption of this definition.

For each integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, define the trace–cup pairing by
$$\langle x,y\rangle_i=\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X(x\smile y):
H^i(X,\Ql)\times H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)\longrightarrow\Ql(-d).$$

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$. Fix a
prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and choose an algebraic
closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$. Let $X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper, and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ be its structure morphism.
Write $H^i(X,-)$ and $H_c^i(X,-)$ for the ordinary and compactly supported
cohomology groups, and, for every integer $m$, write $\Ql(m)$ for the Tate
twist [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] of degree $m$. Write $Ra_X^!$ for
the constructible exceptional inverse image of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] at $\Ql$ and $\Qlb$, which is defined
for every separated finite-type morphism (no admissibility
hypothesis in the sense of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] is
imposed on $a_X$), and $\otimes^L$ for the derived tensor product, using the
derived pullback/tensor/Hom notation. Choose an
orientation isomorphism for the smooth structure morphism $a_X:X\to\Spec k$,

$$
 \eta_X:Ra_X^!\Ql\xrightarrow{\sim}(\Ql)_X(d)[2d],
$$

where $\Ql(d)$ uses the Tate twist [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] of degree $d$. We
use $Ra_{X*}$ and $Ra_{X!}$ for the derived direct image and the
compact-support direct image [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed],
respectively. Through $\eta_X$, the counit $Ra_{X!}Ra_X^!\Ql\to\Ql$ defines
the trace map

$$
 \operatorname{tr}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\Ql(d))\longrightarrow\Ql.
$$

For the proper structure morphism, use the compact-support direct image
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] comparison and, after untwisting, write

$$
 \operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X:H^{2d}(X,\Ql)\longrightarrow\Ql(-d).
$$

The multiplication $(\Ql)_X\otimes^L(\Ql)_X\to(\Ql)_X$ defines, for all
integers $i,j$, cup products

$$
\smile:H^i(X,\Ql)\otimes_{\Ql}H^j(X,\Ql)
 \longrightarrow H^{i+j}(X,\Ql).
$$

For $x\in H^i(X,\Ql)$ and $y\in H^j(X,\Ql)$, the cup product is
graded-commutative:

$$
 y\smile x=(-1)^{ij}x\smile y
 \qquad
 (x\in H^i(X,\Ql),\ y\in H^j(X,\Ql)).
$$

For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, and for every $x\in H^i(X,\Ql)$
and $y\in H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)$, define

$$
 \langle x,y\rangle_i=
 \operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X(x\smile y):
 H^i(X,\Ql)\times H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)
 \longrightarrow\Ql(-d).
$$
